Does paid Fenix growth correlate with organic growth? Segment-level sanity check

Segments: 16 countries × {Fenix organic = total − measured paid, Firefox iOS, Focus Android, Focus iOS}. Paid signal: the country's paid Fenix MAU. Sampled every 28 days (rolling-28 metric). Iran excluded from every statistic (its 2026 is the shutdown). Paid growth is expressed relative to the country's organic Fenix level, so a slope of +0.5 reads "organic grew by half of what paid added".

B. Monthly panel, shared seasonality removed, with lead/lag and a permutation null

Each period's cross-country mean is subtracted from both sides, so anything every country does together (seasonality, releases, the mobile-wide 2026 lift) cannot create the correlation. Lag +1 = paid change in the previous period (paid leads organic); lag −1 = paid change in the next period, which cannot have caused this period's organic change, so a similar value there means the correlation is not causal. The permutation null re-pairs each organic series with a random other country's paid series 500 times, keeping the period structure: permutation_null_r_p95 is the |r| a spurious pairing reaches 5% of the time, permutation_p_value the share of random pairings at least as strong as the real one.

D. The sharper test: organic Fenix growth minus the same country's iOS growth, vs paid added

India and Indonesia are the two biggest spenders, so their being the two outliers is itself the suspicious pattern. Using each country's iOS as the control for local market growth removes the "marketing spends where mobile grows" explanation.

Over the full year the excess is uncorrelated with spend (Spearman −0.25): India's organic Fenix grew less than India's iOS (+17% vs +20%), Brazil's fell 11% while its iOS rose 21% at 50% paid share. Over the high spend period since April the picture changes: India +15 points above its iOS, Indonesia +7, Argentina +6, while Brazil stays −11 (Pearson +0.48, p 0.07; Spearman +0.12).

Month by month: in India organic Fenix tracks iOS almost exactly until June 2026 and then pulls above it through September, as the paid share of Fenix MAU climbs from 25% to 55%. Indonesia's organic Fenix sits above its iOS from March 2026 on the same climb. Brazil and Mexico, at 45–50% paid share, show no such lift. Note Focus Android in Indonesia (+680% over the year) and Germany: Android-ecosystem movements unrelated to Fenix attribution.

Size of what could be bleed. If India's and Indonesia's organic Fenix had grown only at their iOS rate since April, they would be 486,413 MAU lower together, 1.5% of world organic Fenix and 1.0% of world organic mobile MAU.
